- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.27) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.11) over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture mean reversion.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 7-day average.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% per day until reversal.
- If sentiment history includes multiple +0.27 spikes, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% per spike to avoid “overcorrection” bias.
